Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection with a wrist fracture as the primary diagnosis. The
mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported crash, and the findings are in keeping with what would be expected from this
type of force. Radiographs and the clinical examination together clearly confirm the fracture, with tenderness, swelling, and
reduced grip strength documented at initial evaluation. Immobilization was followed by a standard course of rehabilitation,
including range-of-motion and strengthening exercises. Over the course of 21 visits, the patient's pain, mobility, and function
improved steadily, and visit frequency tapered as recovery progressed. A remote history of a minor strain in the same area is
noted in the chart; that episode resolved completely without lasting limitation and does not appear to bear on the current
presentation. Billed services reflect the treatment delivered, with no repeated or duplicate charges identified. At last review the
patient had regained near-full range of motion and was discharged to home exercise with follow-up as needed.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
